findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - `forge land` retries a cancelled lint workflow, and the retry succeeds within a minute. `land.py:64` enables progress caching, and `checks.py:268-270` retains the original cancelled checks for 60 seconds. When the fresh workflow response reports completed attempt 2, this branch leaves those cached checks red even if the retry succeeded, so `_pending` reports a failure and recommends `forge work`. The previous round raised this cancellation classification problem. Its third-party case also remains: lines 345-347 leave a cancelled GitHub App check red when it has no matching Actions workflow. [GitHub's Checks API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/checks/runs?apiVersion=latest) supports checks created by apps. The approved item remains unmet: "When an item's CI checks were cancelled and none failed, close starts them again or waits for the newer run instead of sending the item to a worker round".
findings.title: Not done: Cancelled checks are still reported as failed

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a newer run of the same event is queued before it has published its own check runs. The second proof supplies a separate pending check from the newer suite, so it still passes if the cancelled check is incorrectly marked PASS while the newer workflow is running: that separate check forces the wait. Without that check, the same regression would let close report ready early. Lines 52-53 assert only success and the absence of a rerun; the proof needs to verify waiting when the newer run has not yet reported a job.
